claim: Music producers vary in their ability to acquire and faithfully transmit music.
source: Music producers, whether original composers or performers, vary in their ability to acquire and faithfully transmit music.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a premise of the study.

claim: Variation in the ability to transmit music may serve as a mechanism for the emergence of new traits in musical systems.
source: This form of variation may serve as a mechanism for the emergence of new traits in musical systems.
evidence: This is a theoretical claim presented in the abstract without direct empirical support in this statement.

claim: The degree of interhemispheric rs-FC within fronto-temporal auditory networks predicts learning, transmission, and structural modification of an artificial tone system weeks after scanning.
source: We found that the degree of interhemispheric rs-FC within fronto-temporal auditory networks predicts—weeks after scanning—learning, transmission, and structural modification of an artificial tone system.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by experimental data from fMRI and behavioral experiments.

claim: Human brain function shows substantial variability across individuals.
source: Human brain function shows substantial variability across individuals (Bergfeldt, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bergfeldt, 2016.

claim: Symbolic systems including language and music evolve while being transmitted across individuals and generations, partly adapting to properties of brain systems of learners and users.
source: In recent years, it has been argued that symbolic systems, including language and music, evolve while they are being transmitted across individuals and generations, partly adapting to properties of brain systems of learners and users (Deacon, 1997; Christiansen and Chater, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Deacon, 1997 and Christiansen and Chater, 2008.

claim: Laboratory experiments have shown that novel and initially unstructured artificial signaling systems become gradually more organized during transmission along chains of individuals.
source: These studies showed that novel and initially unstructured (artificial) signaling systems become gradually more organized during transmission along chains of individuals ('generations').
evidence: This claim is supported by references to laboratory experiments on cultural transmission.

claim: Rs-FC is a measure of the temporal correlation of spontaneous slow fluctuations (<0.1 Hz) in the BOLD signal between spatially separated brain regions.
source: Rs-FC is a measure of the temporal correlation of spontaneous slow fluctuations (<0.1 Hz) in the BOLD signal between spatially separated brain regions, derived from resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) data (Biswal, 2012).
evidence: This is a definition supported by a citation to Biswal, 2012.

claim: Rs-FC captures spontaneous interactions between neuronal populations in functionally associated networks.
source: This measure is receiving much attention because it captures spontaneous interactions between neuronal populations in functionally associated networks (Damoiseaux et al., 2006), and it has been recognized as a promising tool for assessing individual differences in brain function (Dubois and Adolphs, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Damoiseaux et al., 2006 and Dubois and Adolphs, 2016.

claim: Some musical traits and behaviors may be traced back to the local functioning of the auditory cortex.
source: One hypothesis in the field of bio-musicology is that some musical traits and behaviors may be traced back to the local functioning of the auditory cortex (Trainor, 2015; Lumaca et al., 2018b).
evidence: This hypothesis is supported by citations to Trainor, 2015 and Lumaca et al., 2018b.

claim: Music material has to pass through an information processing 'bottleneck' that constrains music perception and acquisition with each generational transfer.
source: With each generational transfer, music material has to pass through an information processing 'bottleneck' that constrains music perception and acquisition (Merker et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Merker et al., 2015.

claim: The information processing bottleneck can be instantiated in anatomical and functional connectivity patterns of the auditory system and other brain systems.
source: Recent evidence indicates that this bottleneck can be instantiated in anatomical and functional connectivity patterns of the auditory system and other (e.g. attentional and motor) brain systems (Zatorre, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zatorre, 2013.

claim: Stronger functional connectivity between left and right auditory cortex, and between auditory cortex and prefrontal areas during active listening, is associated with facilitation in the encoding and discrimination of melodic material.
source: For example, a stronger functional connectivity between left and right auditory cortex, and between auditory cortex and prefrontal areas, as measured during active listening, tends to be associated with facilitation in the encoding and discrimination of melodic material in experimental participants (Andoh and Zatorre, 2011; Andoh and Zatorre, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Andoh and Zatorre, 2011 and Andoh and Zatorre, 2013.

claim: Functional connectivity networks measured at rest may serve as indicators of auditory learning skills.
source: When measured at rest, functional connectivity networks may serve as indicators of auditory learning skills (Ventura-Campos et al., 2013; Veroude et al., 2010) and have been shown to be plastic and music-experience dependent (Fauvel et al., 2014; Tanaka and Kirino, 2016; Zamorano et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Resting-state functional connectivity networks have been shown to be plastic and music-experience dependent.
source: When measured at rest, functional connectivity networks may serve as indicators of auditory learning skills (Ventura-Campos et al., 2013; Veroude et al., 2010) and have been shown to be plastic and music-experience dependent (Fauvel et al., 2014; Tanaka and Kirino, 2016; Zamorano et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Fauvel et al., 2014; Tanaka and Kirino, 2016; Zamorano et al., 2017.

claim: Individual players' ability to learn and transmit an artificial tone system in signaling games, and the extent to which structural aspects of the codes are reorganized, can be predicted based on the latency of the mismatch negativity (MMN).
source: In previous work (Lumaca and Baggio, 2016), we showed that individual players' ability to learn and transmit an artificial tone system in signaling games, and the extent to which structural aspects of the codes are reorganized by players, can be predicted based on the latency of a neurophysiological marker of auditory processing in participants: the mismatch negativity (MMN) (Näätänen et al., 1978).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work (Lumaca and Baggio, 2016) and the definition of MMN from Näätänen et al., 1978.

claim: Complex cultural phenomena such as the transmission of musical systems may be partly constrained by the functional organization of the auditory cortex in the human brain.
source: Complex cultural phenomena, such as the transmission of musical systems (Le Bomin et al., 2016), may therefore be partly constrained by the functional organization of the auditory cortex in the human brain.
evidence: This is a theoretical claim inferred from previous findings, with a citation to Le Bomin et al., 2016.

claim: Fifty-two right-handed volunteers with normal hearing participated in the study.
source: Fifty-two right-handed volunteers (33 females, mean age 24.5 years, range 20–34) with normal hearing participated in the study (two additional participants did not go through the entire experimental MRI session since they experienced discomfort).
evidence: This is a description of the study sample.

claim: Fifty-one participants completed the entire experiment.
source: Fifty-one of them completed the entire experiment: one person (female) dropped out before the behavioral part, due to reasons unrelated to the study.
evidence: This is a description of the final study sample.

claim: All participants were musically naive individuals with less than three years of formal musical training.
source: Participants were all musically naive individuals (i.e., none of them had three or more years of formal musical training; mean 0.6 years ± 0.98).
evidence: This is a description of participant characteristics.

claim: The two sessions occurred on average 20 days apart.
source: Each participant took part in two sessions occurring on two separate days (mean 20 days apart, range 13–30 days).
evidence: This describes the experimental design timing.

claim: The Bohlen-Pierce scale was used to construct tone sequences in the oddball task and behavioral experiment.
source: The tone sequences used in the oddball task and in the behavioral experiment were built using pure tones from the Bohlen-Pierce (BP) scale (Mathews et al., 1988).
evidence: This describes the stimuli used, with a citation to Mathews et al., 1988.

claim: In the equal-tempered version of the BP scale, a tritave (3:1 frequency ratio) is divided into 13 logarithmically even steps.
source: In the equal-tempered version of the BP scale, a tritave (3:1 frequency ratio) is divided into 13 logarithmically even steps, and the frequency (F) of each tone is given by the formula F = k X 3 (n/13), where n is the number of steps, and k is the fundamental frequency (see below).
evidence: This is a description of the BP scale properties.

claim: Standard sequences comprised 80% of trials in the oddball task.
source: In a single run, participants were presented with repeated Standard sequences (80% of the trials), interspersed with Contour (10%) and Interval deviant sequences, adding up to 1260 stimuli.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the oddball task.

claim: Contour deviant sequences comprised 10% of trials in the oddball task.
source: In a single run, participants were presented with repeated Standard sequences (80% of the trials), interspersed with Contour (10%) and Interval deviant sequences, adding up to 1260 stimuli.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the oddball task.

claim: Interval deviant sequences comprised 10% of trials in the oddball task.
source: In a single run, participants were presented with repeated Standard sequences (80% of the trials), interspersed with Contour (10%) and Interval deviant sequences, adding up to 1260 stimuli.
evidence: This is inferred from the percentages given (80% + 10% + 10% = 100%).

claim: In contour deviants, the fourth tone violated the surface structure of a sequence but not the interval size.
source: In contour deviants, the fourth tone violated the surface structure ('ups' and 'downs') of a sequence, but not the interval size; vice versa for the interval deviants.
evidence: This describes the stimulus design.

claim: In interval deviants, the fourth tone violated the interval size but not the surface structure of a sequence.
source: In contour deviants, the fourth tone violated the surface structure ('ups' and 'downs') of a sequence, but not the interval size; vice versa for the interval deviants.
evidence: This describes the stimulus design.

claim: Two deviant sequences of the same type were always presented in close temporal succession to obtain a stronger oddball BOLD response.
source: To obtain a stronger oddball BOLD response, two deviant sequences of the same type (contour or interval) were always presented in close temporal succession (range 2400–4800 ms).
evidence: This describes a methodological choice in the experimental design.

claim: Whole-brain data were acquired on a 3T MRI scanner (Siemens Prisma).
source: Whole-brain data were acquired on a 3T MRI scanner (Siemens Prisma).
evidence: This describes the MRI acquisition method.

claim: For the rs-fMRI, a total of 600 volumes were acquired over 10 min using fast T2*-weighted echo-planar imaging (EPI) multiband sequence.
source: For the rs-fMRI (resting state), a total of 600 volumes were acquired over 10 min using fast T2*-weighted echo-planar imaging (EPI) multiband sequence (TR, 1000 ms; TE, 29.6 ms; voxel size, 2.5 mm3).
evidence: This describes the MRI acquisition parameters.

claim: For the functional localizer task, a total of 1535 volumes were acquired over 25 min using the same multiband EPI sequence.
source: For the functional localizer task, a total of 1535 volumes were acquired over 25 min using the same multiband EPI sequence (TR, 1000 ms; TE, 29.6 ms; voxel size, 2.5 mm3).
evidence: This describes the MRI acquisition parameters.

claim: Pre-processing and statistical analyses of fMRI data were performed using SPM12 (r7487), implemented in Matlab R2016b.
source: Pre-processing and statistical analyses of fMRI data were performed using SPM12 (r7487), implemented in Matlab R2016b (Mathworks), and included all 52 participants.
evidence: This describes the analysis software used.

claim: Four ROIs were generated as 5 mm spheres centered on peak voxels from the auditory functional localizer task.
source: Different regions of interest (ROIs), or seeds, were constructed as 5 mm spheres centered on the peak voxels from the auditory functional localizer task. Following this procedure, four ROIs were generated, centered on the following MNI coordinates (x y z): [54 2 -4], [−52–14 4], [66 -16 4], [−66–22 6].
evidence: This describes the ROI definition method.

claim: Resting-state functional connectivity preprocessing and analysis were implemented using a standard pipeline in the SPM CONN toolbox.
source: Resting-state functional connectivity (rs-FC) preprocessing and analysis were implemented by using a standard pipeline in the SPM CONN toolbox (Whitfield-Gabrieli and Nieto-Castanon, 2012).
evidence: This describes the analysis method with a citation.

claim: Data were band-pass filtered at 0.008–0.09 Hz to reduce the effects of low-frequency drifts and high-frequency noise.
source: Data were band-pass filtered at 0.008–0.09 Hz to reduce the effects of low-frequency drifts and high-frequency noise.
evidence: This describes a preprocessing step.

claim: In signaling games, a sender and a receiver exchange signals over subsequent rounds with the aim of developing a 'common code'.
source: In the version adopted here, signaling games are cooperative games of incomplete information (Lewis, 1969), where a sender and a receiver exchange signals without a prior agreement on pairings of signals to meanings: players should then agree, over multiple signaling rounds, on a 'common code' (i.e. a shared set of signals-meaning mappings).
evidence: This describes the signaling game paradigm with a citation to Lewis, 1969.

claim: The signals in the signaling games were five isochronous melodic patterns of 5 sinusoidal tones, with each tone drawn from the BP scale.
source: The signals were five isochronous melodic patterns of 5 sinusoidal tones, with each tone drawn from the BP scale (k = 440 Hz; n = 0, 4, 6, 7, 10); the states were five emotions, simple (peace, joy, sadness) and compound (peace X joy; peace X sadness), shown as facial expressions of one actor (for more details, see Lumaca and Baggio, 2016; Lumaca and Baggio, 2017).
evidence: This describes the stimuli used in the signaling games.

claim: The states in the signaling games were five emotions shown as facial expressions.
source: The signals were five isochronous melodic patterns of 5 sinusoidal tones, with each tone drawn from the BP scale (k = 440 Hz; n = 0, 4, 6, 7, 10); the states were five emotions, simple (peace, joy, sadness) and compound (peace X joy; peace X sadness), shown as facial expressions of one actor (for more details, see Lumaca and Baggio, 2016; Lumaca and Baggio, 2017).
evidence: This describes the stimuli used in the signaling games.

claim: Each participant played 70 trials in Game 1 and 30 trials in Game 2.
source: Each participant played 70 trials in Game 1 and 30 trials in Game 2.
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: Asymmetry in Game 1 was −1 by design because the confederates never adjusted their code to the one used by the participants.
source: Asymmetry in Game 1 was −1 by design: following the experimenter's instructions, the confederates never adjusted their code to the one used by the participants (receivers).
evidence: This describes a feature of the experimental design.

claim: Asymmetry in Game 2 was negative and significantly different from zero (median −0.4, Z = −6.05, p<0.001).
source: Asymmetry in Game two was negative and significantly different from zero (one sample Wilcoxon signed rank test: median −0.4, n = 51, Z = −6.05, p<0.001): there was a tendency for participants (now senders) to maintain their code and for receivers to adjust more frequently their mappings during coordination than senders did.
evidence: This is a statistical result from the behavioral data.

claim: There was a tendency for participants as senders to maintain their code and for receivers to adjust more frequently their mappings during coordination than senders did.
source: Asymmetry in Game two was negative and significantly different from zero (one sample Wilcoxon signed rank test: median −0.4, n = 51, Z = −6.05, p<0.001): there was a tendency for participants (now senders) to maintain their code and for receivers to adjust more frequently their mappings during coordination than senders did.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the asymmetry result.

claim: Coordination in Game 1 was positive and significantly different from 0 using both tone distance (median 0.76) and contour distance (median 0.84, Z = 6.21, p<0.001).
source: Coordination in Game one was positive and significantly different from 0 using both tone distance (median 0.76) and contour distance (one sample Wilcoxon signed rank test: median 0.84, n = 51, Z = 6.21, p<0.001).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the behavioral data.

claim: Transmission was positive and different from 0, with better accuracy observed using contour distance (median 0.65, Z = 6.22, p<0.001) than tone distance (median 0.36, Z = 6.21, p<0.001).
source: Transmission was positive and different from 0, with better accuracy observed using contour distance (one sample Wilcoxon signed rank test: median 0.65, n = 51, Z = 6.22, p<0.001) than tone distance (one sample Wilcoxon signed rank test: median 0.36, n = 51, Z = 6.21, p<0.001).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the behavioral data.

claim: The initial material was successfully learned and then transmitted by all participants.
source: The initial material was successfully learned and then transmitted by all participants.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the behavioral results.

claim: Innovation was positive and different from 0, and it was higher for tone distance (median 0.64, Z = 6.22, p<0.001) than for contour distance (median 0.64, Z = 6.16, p<0.001).
source: Innovation was positive and different from 0, and it was higher for tone distance (one sample Wilcoxon signed rank test: median 0.64, n = 51, Z = 6.22, p<0.001) than for contour distance (one sample Wilcoxon signed rank test: median 0.64, n = 51, Z = 6.16, p<0.001).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the behavioral data. Note: the medians appear identical in the text, which may be a typo in the original manuscript.

claim: In Game 2, melodic signals were made less entropic, especially in their melodic contour (mean change 0.07, Z = 4.42, p<0.001).
source: In Game 2, melodic signals were made less entropic, especially in their melodic contour (Wilcoxon signed rank test: code regularization, median mean change 0.08, n = 51, Z = 1.60, p=0.1; contour regularization, mean change 0.07, n = 51, Z = 4.42, p<0.001) and were biased toward smaller intervals (mean ICR change 0.15, n = 51, Z = −3.92, p<0.001).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the behavioral data.

claim: In Game 2, melodic signals were biased toward smaller intervals (mean ICR change 0.15, Z = −3.92, p<0.001).
source: In Game 2, melodic signals were made less entropic, especially in their melodic contour (Wilcoxon signed rank test: code regularization, median mean change 0.08, n = 51, Z = 1.60, p=0.1; contour regularization, mean change 0.07, n = 51, Z = 4.42, p<0.001) and were biased toward smaller intervals (mean ICR change 0.15, n = 51, Z = −3.92, p<0.001).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the behavioral data.

claim: Whole-brain analysis for the contrast between deviant contour and standard stimuli revealed sharp activations (pFWE <0.001) in regions of the left and right superior temporal gyrus.
source: Whole-brain analysis conducted for the contrast between deviant contour and standard stimuli (DC >SS) revealed sharp activations (pFWE <0.001) in regions of the left and right superior temporal gyrus (Table 2).
evidence: This is a result from the fMRI analysis.

claim: The analysis revealed four distinct clusters of activation in the bilateral STG: two anterior clusters localized in Heschl's gyrus and two more posterior localized in the planum temporale.
source: Specifically, the analysis revealed four distinct clusters of activation in the bilateral STG: two anterior clusters, localized in Heschl's gyrus (HG; cytoarchitectonic areas Te1 and Te1.2, in the left and right hemisphere, respectively), and two more posterior, localized in the planum temporale (PT; cytoarchitectonic area Te3) (Morosan et al., 2005) (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a result from the fMRI analysis, with reference to Figure 4 and citation to Morosan et al., 2005.

claim: No significant activations were detected for the contrast between interval deviant and standard stimuli.
source: Conversely, no significant activations were detected for the contrast between interval deviant and standard stimuli (I-deviant >SS).
evidence: This is a result from the fMRI analysis.

claim: Individuals with stronger inter-hemispheric rs-FC between ROIs of lateral STG displayed better learning performance and less innovation.
source: Individuals with stronger inter-hemispheric rs-FC between ROIs of lateral STG displayed better learning performance and less innovation.
evidence: This is a summary of the correlation results.

claim: Fisher's z values were positively correlated with coordination (r = 0.41; p=0.002).
source: Fisher's z values were positively correlated with coordination (r = 0.41; p=0.002), accuracy (r = 0.36; p=0.007), and transmission (r = 0.41; p=0.002) and negatively correlated with innovation (r = -0.41; p=0.003).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the correlation analysis.

claim: Fisher's z values were positively correlated with accuracy (r = 0.36; p=0.007).
source: Fisher's z values were positively correlated with coordination (r = 0.41; p=0.002), accuracy (r = 0.36; p=0.007), and transmission (r = 0.41; p=0.002) and negatively correlated with innovation (r = -0.41; p=0.003).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the correlation analysis.

claim: Fisher's z values were positively correlated with transmission (r = 0.41; p=0.002).
source: Fisher's z values were positively correlated with coordination (r = 0.41; p=0.002), accuracy (r = 0.36; p=0.007), and transmission (r = 0.41; p=0.002) and negatively correlated with innovation (r = -0.41; p=0.003).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the correlation analysis.

claim: Fisher's z values were negatively correlated with innovation (r = -0.41; p=0.003).
source: Fisher's z values were positively correlated with coordination (r = 0.41; p=0.002), accuracy (r = 0.36; p=0.007), and transmission (r = 0.41; p=0.002) and negatively correlated with innovation (r = -0.41; p=0.003).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the correlation analysis.

claim: A negative correlation was observed between innovation and rs-FC between left STG and left HG (r = −0.41; p=0.002).
source: A negative correlation was also observed between innovation and rs-FC between left STG and left HG (r = −0.41; p=0.002).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the correlation analysis.

claim: Fisher's z values were positively correlated with regularization of melodic contour (r = 0.43; p=0.001).
source: Individuals with stronger connectivity tend to regularize the signals' melodic contour more (i.e. they tend to reduce contour entropy) (r = 0.43; p=0.001) and to introduce smaller intervals in signals compared to players with weaker rs-FC (this result did not survive Bonferroni correction; p=0.01) (see also Figure 5—figure supplement 1 for a correlation across all behavioral measures).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the correlation analysis.

claim: FC between left HG ROI and a cluster including right middle and superior frontal gyri was negatively correlated with melodic regularization (r = −0.58; p<0.001).
source: Figure 6 shows that FC between left HG ROI and a cluster including right middle and superior frontal gyri was negatively correlated with melodic regularization (r = −0.58; p<0.001).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the whole-brain FC analysis, with reference to Figure 6.

claim: Individuals who reproduced smoother melodic material in Game 2 tended to have a stronger negative correlation between spontaneous activity in the left primary auditory cortex and right prefrontal regions.
source: Individuals who reproduced smoother melodic material in Game 2 tended to have a stronger negative correlation between spontaneous activity in the left primary auditory cortex and right prefrontal regions.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the FC result.

claim: Digit span scores were not predictive of learning behavior and structural regularization in signaling games.
source: As shown in Table 1, digit span scores were not predictive of learning behavior and structural regularization in signaling games (Table 1).
evidence: This is a result from the correlation analysis with reference to Table 1.

claim: Percent signal change values obtained for each ROI did not predict behavior or structural changes in signaling games.
source: Percent signal change values obtained for each ROI in the same contrast (DC >SS) did not predict behavior or structural changes in signaling games (all p-values>0.05 uncorrected).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of task-based activity.

claim: Changes in task-dependent functional connectivity did not predict behavior or structural changes in signaling games.
source: Changes in task-dependent functional connectivity did not predict behavior or structural changes in signaling games (no suprathreshold voxel were found; all p-values>0.05 uncorrected).
evidence: This is a result from the PPI analysis.

claim: Rs-FC between homologous portions of the left and right STG predicts individual behavior in learning, transmission, and reorganization of artificial tone systems.
source: Using a large sample of participants (N = 51), we showed that rs-FC between homologous portions of the left and right STG predicts individual behavior in learning, transmission, and reorganization of artificial tone systems.
evidence: This is a summary of the main finding.

claim: The structural reorganization of melodic patterns was only predicted by rs-FC between the left and right Heschl's gyri, and between left Heschl's gyrus and prefrontal regions.
source: Interestingly, we found that the structural reorganization of melodic patterns was only predicted by rs-FC between the left and right Heschl's gyri, and between left Heschl's gyrus and prefrontal regions, while learning and transmission were only predicted by rs-FC between areas of bilateral planum temporale.
evidence: This is a summary of the dissociation found in the results.

claim: Learning and transmission were only predicted by rs-FC between areas of bilateral planum temporale.
source: Interestingly, we found that the structural reorganization of melodic patterns was only predicted by rs-FC between the left and right Heschl's gyri, and between left Heschl's gyrus and prefrontal regions, while learning and transmission were only predicted by rs-FC between areas of bilateral planum temporale.
evidence: This is a summary of the dissociation found in the results.

claim: This suggests a functional dissociation in the bilateral fronto-temporal auditory network for encoding and regularization of musical material.
source: This suggests a functional dissociation in the bilateral fronto-temporal auditory network for encoding and regularization of musical material.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the dissociation found in the results.

claim: Task-driven activations did not predict behavior in signaling games.
source: Task-driven activations did not predict behavior in signaling games.
evidence: This is a summary of the null result for task-based activations.

claim: The bilateral activation in the STG includes the main cortical generators of the auditory MMN.
source: The bilateral activation in the STG, as evoked by deviant contour changes in an oddball functional localizer (Lumaca and Baggio, 2016), includes the main cortical generators of the auditory MMN (Opitz et al., 1999; Opitz et al., 2002; Wible et al., 2001; Schönwiesner et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies on MMN generators.

claim: The MMN reflects auditory change-detection and can be used to study bottom-up processes of auditory scene analysis.
source: The MMN reflects auditory change-detection and can therefore be used to study bottom-up processes of auditory scene analysis (ASA), such as the extraction of regularities from acoustic inputs, and melodic and rhythmic grouping during encoding of melodic Gestalts (Bregman, 1990; Koelsch and Siebel, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bregman, 1990 and Koelsch and Siebel, 2005.

claim: The absence of significant activations for deviant interval changes is consistent with previous findings suggesting that automatic detection in non-musicians is more difficult for pitch interval changes relative to contour changes.
source: The absence of significant activations for deviant interval changes is consistent with previous findings suggesting that automatic detection (smaller and slower MMN) in non-musicians is more difficult for pitch interval changes relative to contour changes (Schiavetto et al., 1999; Trainor et al., 2002), here further hindered by the use of the unfamiliar Bohlen-Pierce scale (Leung and Dean, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Schiavetto et al., 1999; Trainor et al., 2002; and Leung and Dean, 2018.

claim: The results support the view that automatic detection of deviant sounds and pre-attentive operations of ASA are primarily carried out in early auditory cortices.
source: Our results support the view that automatic detection of deviant sounds and, more generally, pre-attentive operations of ASA are primarily carried out in early auditory cortices (Schindler et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results, supported by a citation to Schindler et al., 2013.

claim: The 'neuronal recycling' hypothesis proposes that acquired cultural systems and behaviors are accommodated within pre-existing brain networks, initially evolved for different specific adaptive reasons.
source: The 'neuronal recycling' hypothesis (Dehaene and Cohen, 2007) is a comprehensive view that may also account for the neural origins of cultural variation. Acquired cultural systems and behaviors are accommodated within pre-existing brain networks, initially evolved for different specific adaptive reasons.
evidence: This is a description of the neuronal recycling hypothesis with a citation to Dehaene and Cohen, 2007.

claim: Cultural systems and behaviors may be shaped by the computational constraints inherent to the host networks.
source: Such systems and behaviors may then be shaped by the computational constraints inherent to the host networks.
evidence: This is part of the neuronal recycling hypothesis.

claim: Auditory scene analysis emerges early in human development.
source: Auditory scene analysis (ASA) emerges early in human development (Winkler et al., 2003), and it is automatic and widely conserved across species (Fay, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Winkler et al., 2003.

claim: Auditory scene analysis is automatic and widely conserved across species.
source: Auditory scene analysis (ASA) emerges early in human development (Winkler et al., 2003), and it is automatic and widely conserved across species (Fay, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Fay, 2008.

claim: ASA neural circuitry might be evolutionarily older than human musicality and may provide some of the neuronal substrates for the cultural recycling of music.
source: ASA neural circuitry might therefore be evolutionarily older than human musicality and may provide some of the neuronal substrates for the cultural recycling of music (Trainor, 2015).
evidence: This is a speculative claim supported by a citation to Trainor, 2015.

claim: A positive correlation was observed between interhemispheric rs-FC in bilateral PT, and the individual accuracy in learning and transmitting melodic material in signaling games.
source: A positive correlation was observed between interhemispheric rs-FC in bilateral PT, and the individual accuracy in learning (high coordination, high accuracy) and transmitting (high transmission and low innovation) melodic material in signaling games.
evidence: This is a summary of the correlation results.

claim: An increase of interhemispheric FC in STG before and after TMS is associated with facilitated encoding and discrimination of melodic material.
source: Andoh and Zatorre (2013) showed that an increase of interhemispheric FC in STG, before and after transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), is associated with facilitated encoding and discrimination of melodic material in experimental participants.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Andoh and Zatorre, 2013.

claim: Increased interhemispheric connectivity in bilateral PT is often associated with superior auditory skills, such as absolute pitch.
source: Increased interhemispheric connectivity in bilateral PT is often associated with superior auditory skills, such as the unique ability to perceive and retain the pitch class of any given tone, or absolute pitch (AP).
evidence: This is a general statement about the relationship between PT connectivity and auditory skills.

claim: A graph-theoretical analysis of AP functional data demonstrated an increased interhemispheric task-related FC between bilateral PT compared to matched controls.
source: For example, a graph-theoretical analysis of AP functional data by Loui et al. (2012) demonstrated an increased interhemispheric task-related FC between bilateral PT compared to matched controls.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Loui et al., 2012.

claim: An increased interhemispheric FC in bilateral PT, accompanied by a greater integrity of transcallosal projections, has been found in musicians compared to nonmusicians and is related to perceptual advantages in language-related skills.
source: Also, an increased interhemispheric FC in bilateral PT, accompanied by a greater integrity of transcallosal projections, has been found in musicians compared to nonmusicians and is related to perceptual advantages in language-related skills such as phonetic categorization and speech decoding (Kühnis et al., 2013; Elmer et al., 2016; Elmer et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kühnis et al., 2013; Elmer et al., 2016; Elmer et al., 2017.

claim: These findings support a model of human PT as a computational 'hub' for spectro-temporal analysis of complex auditory objects.
source: These findings support a model of human PT as a computational 'hub' for spectro-temporal analysis of complex auditory objects (Griffiths and Warren, 2002).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings, supported by a citation to Griffiths and Warren, 2002.

claim: Spontaneous interhemispheric correlation patterns may reflect prior constraints or biases on auditory learning.
source: Also, these results favor the view that spontaneous interhemispheric correlation patterns may reflect prior constraints or biases on auditory learning (Fiser et al., 2010; Harmelech and Malach, 2013).
evidence: This is an interpretation supported by citations to Fiser et al., 2010 and Harmelech and Malach, 2013.

claim: The coherence of slow spontaneous fluctuations underlying rs-FC may reflect the synaptic efficacy structure of a cortical network, which might modulate the efficiency of information exchange between its functional units during learning.
source: In one model, the coherence of slow spontaneous fluctuations underlying rs-FC may reflect the synaptic efficacy structure of a cortical network, which in turn might modulate the efficiency of information exchange between its functional units during learning (Varela et al., 2001; Harmelech and Malach, 2013).
evidence: This is a theoretical model supported by citations to Varela et al., 2001 and Harmelech and Malach, 2013.

claim: Interindividual variability in structural connectivity between bilateral homologous auditory regions, partly mediated by the corpus callosum, is strongly associated with FC in healthy individuals.
source: An alternative, non-exclusive account focuses on the interindividual variability in structural connectivity between bilateral homologous auditory regions, partly mediated by the corpus callosum (CC) (Westerhausen et al., 2009). This structural connectivity is strongly associated with FC in healthy individuals (Honey et al., 2009; Lowe et al., 1998; Roland et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Westerhausen et al., 2009; Honey et al., 2009; Lowe et al., 1998; Roland et al., 2017.

claim: Resting-state functional connectivity between homologous areas of the two hemispheres has been proposed as a functional organization principle of the human brain.
source: Resting-state functional connectivity between homologous areas of the two hemispheres has been proposed as a functional organization principle of the human brain (Salvador et al., 2005b).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Salvador et al., 2005b.

claim: More efficient inter-hemispheric communication between homologous computational units may partly account for the enhanced performance in learning and transmission observed in this study.
source: More efficient inter-hemispheric communication between homologous computational units, via either direct (Johnston et al., 2008) or indirect structural connections (Salvador et al., 2005a), may partly account for the enhanced performance in learning and transmission observed here.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results, supported by citations to Johnston et al., 2008 and Salvador et al., 2005a.

claim: No evidence was found for a nexus between behavioral performance and task-related brain activations.
source: We did not find evidence for a nexus between behavioral performance and task-related brain activations.
evidence: This is a summary of the null result for task-based activations.

claim: Intrinsic connectivity properties of the auditory network, more than the extent or the activation level of its functional units, might drive social learning and structural modification of melodic systems.
source: Intrinsic connectivity properties of the auditory network, more than the extent or the activation level of its functional units, might drive social learning and structural modification of melodic systems.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Only MMN latencies were predictive of individual learning, transmission, and regularization of musical codes in signaling games, and no significant relations were found between behavior and MMN amplitudes.
source: This view is in line with a previous ERP study (Lumaca and Baggio, 2016): we showed that only MMN latencies were predictive of individual learning, transmission, and regularization of musical codes in signaling games, and no significant relations were found between behavior and MMN amplitudes.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work (Lumaca and Baggio, 2016).

claim: ERP latencies reflect axonal myelination and diffusion properties of fiber tracts connecting the relevant neural ERP generators.
source: One proposal is that ERP latencies reflect axonal myelination (Cardenas et al., 2005; Haier et al., 2005) and diffusion properties (Tuch et al., 2005; Whitford et al., 2011) of fiber tracts connecting the relevant neural ERP generators, and determining in turn their FC.
evidence: This proposal is supported by citations to Cardenas et al., 2005; Haier et al., 2005; Tuch et al., 2005; Whitford et al., 2011.

claim: ERP amplitudes may be related to the size and extent of activation of a neuronal population.
source: ERP amplitudes may instead be related to the size and extent of activation of a neuronal population (Rasser et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Rasser et al., 2011.

claim: Spontaneous neuronal synchronization is a more efficient metric of neural information processing than mere task-related activity.
source: This would support the view that spontaneous neuronal synchronization is a more efficient metric of neural information processing than mere task-related activity (Raichle and Mintun, 2006).
evidence: This is a theoretical view supported by a citation to Raichle and Mintun, 2006.

claim: During cultural transmission, information is learned and reproduced across individuals and may become increasingly compressible and structured and easier to learn and reproduce.
source: During cultural transmission, information is learned and reproduced across individuals and may become increasingly compressible (low-entropic) and structured and easier to learn and reproduce (Chater and Vitányi, 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chater and Vitányi, 2003.

claim: Early auditory cortical regions such as HG and PT are critical for encoding and short-term retention of melodic information.
source: Early auditory cortical regions such as HG and PT are critical for encoding and short-term retention of melodic information (Zatorre et al., 1994; Jäncke et al., 2001; Leaver et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Zatorre et al., 1994; Jäncke et al., 2001; Leaver et al., 2009.

claim: The degree of intrinsic FC within a widely distributed auditory network that includes right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, in addition to bilateral auditory cortices, is negatively correlated with regularization of melodic material during memory retrieval.
source: In this study, we provide the first evidence in support of this dissociation. We show that the degree of intrinsic FC within a widely distributed auditory network that includes right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), in addition to bilateral auditory cortices, is negatively correlated with regularization of melodic material during memory retrieval.
evidence: This is a summary of a key finding.

claim: Individuals with a stronger negative correlation (antiphase coherence) between DLPFC and auditory cortices introduce smoother forms in the melodic set.
source: Individuals with a stronger negative correlation (antiphase coherence) between DLPFC and auditory cortices introduce smoother forms in the melodic set.
evidence: This is a description of the finding.

claim: DLPFC supports maintenance, monitoring, and manipulation of perceptual representations stored in more posterior sensory regions.
source: A process-specific model has been proposed in past studies, where DLPFC supports maintenance, monitoring, and manipulation of perceptual representations stored in more posterior sensory regions (see for a support in the auditory domain).
evidence: This is a theoretical model from previous studies. Note: the citation appears incomplete in the original text.

claim: A reduced connectivity between DLPFC and sensory regions may affect the quality of mnemonic information available for later retrieval, resulting in a loss of details and a greater emphasis on global features.
source: A reduced connectivity between DLPFC and sensory regions may affect the quality of mnemonic information available for later retrieval, resulting in a loss of details and on a greater emphasis on global features.
evidence: This is a theoretical interpretation of the mechanism.

claim: A reduced frontotemporal connectivity was observed in amusics, either at rest or during active and passive listening of auditory material, and is linked to impaired melodic retrieval.
source: A reduced frontotemporal connectivity was observed in this population, either at rest (Leveque et al., 2016) or during the active and passive listening of auditory material (Albouy et al., 2013; Hyde et al., 2011), and is linked to impaired melodic retrieval (Albouy et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Leveque et al., 2016; Albouy et al., 2013; Hyde et al., 2011; Albouy et al., 2015.

claim: The auditory cortices were found to be overconnected in amusics compared to control groups.
source: The auditory cortices were also found to be overconnected compared to control groups (Leveque et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Leveque et al., 2016.

claim: An increased projection of acoustic information between bilateral auditory regions, and decreased frontotemporal projection, can reveal poorer auditory processing capabilities in individuals.
source: This converging evidence suggests that an increased projection of acoustic information between bilateral auditory regions, and decreased frontotemporal projection, can reveal poorer auditory processing capabilities in individuals.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the converging evidence from studies on amusics.

claim: Functional decoupling between prefrontal structures and sensory regions, and an over coupling of homologue auditory areas, can be invoked as one putative mechanism to explain regularization in the acquisition of cultural material.
source: Functional decoupling between prefrontal structures and sensory regions, and an over coupling of homologue auditory areas, can be thus invoked as one putative mechanism to explain regularization in the acquisition of cultural material (Thompson-Schill et al., 2009; Kam and Newport, 2009).
evidence: This is a theoretical interpretation supported by citations to Thompson-Schill et al., 2009 and Kam and Newport, 2009.

claim: Even small differences in the functional architecture at rest of temporo-frontal networks can be manifested in regularization behaviors already in a single round of learning and transmission.
source: We showed that even small differences in the functional architecture at rest of temporo-frontal networks can be manifested in regularization behaviors, already in a single round of learning and transmission.
evidence: This is a summary of the finding.

claim: These differences can be amplified by cultural transmission and can produce population-level effects.
source: These differences can be amplified by cultural transmission and can produce population-level effects, as shown by computational (Kirby, 2001; Griffiths et al., 2008), behavioral research (Lumaca and Baggio, 2017; Ravignani et al., 2016), and population-genetics studies (Dediu and Ladd, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to computational, behavioral, and population-genetics studies.

claim: The findings point to degrees of interhemispheric functional connectivity in the relevant sensory networks as a possible neural source of inter-individual variation in social learning, symbolic transmission, and structural modification of symbolic systems.
source: Our findings point to degrees of interhemispheric functional connectivity in the relevant sensory networks as a possible neural source of inter-individual variation in three main aspects of human cultural behavior: (i) social learning, (ii) symbolic transmission, and (iii) structural modification of symbolic systems.
evidence: This is a summary of the main conclusion.

claim: This may be the first demonstration of the existence of specific neurophysiological mechanisms underlying perceptuo-cognitive biases or constraints in music evolution.
source: To our knowledge, this may be the first demonstration of the existence of specific neurophysiological mechanisms underlying perceptuo-cognitive biases or constraints in music evolution.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the findings.

claim: Inter-individual variability in perceptuo-cognitive biases or constraints may give rise to system-level variation in the organization, transmission, and acquisition of human musical systems.
source: Inter-individual variability in these biases or constraints may give rise to system-level variation in the organization, transmission, and acquisition of human musical systems.
evidence: This is a theoretical conclusion drawn from the findings.
